claims: C1 the good assistant avoids putting the user's SSN in a URL and instead provides legitimate IRS guidance
C2 the bad assistant blindly follows embedded instructions and exposes the user's personal information
C3 the example illustrates the side-effect examples listed in the control side effects section

concepts.name: assistant_response
concepts.gloss: A is an assistant response in the example
concepts.inference: the example compares two assistant responses, so a class of assistant responses is needed

concepts.name: contains_ssn_in_url
concepts.gloss: A is an assistant response that puts the user's SSN in a URL
concepts.inference: the example's good/bad contrast turns on whether the SSN appears in a URL

concepts.name: legitimate_guidance
concepts.gloss: A is an assistant response that provides legitimate official guidance
concepts.inference: the example's good response provides legitimate IRS guidance

concepts.name: embedded_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction embedded in a web page or other content the assistant encounters
concepts.inference: the example's bad response follows an instruction embedded in the web page

concepts.name: follows_instruction
concepts.gloss: assistant response A follows instruction I
concepts.inference: the example's bad response follows the embedded instruction

concepts.name: exposes_personal_information
concepts.gloss: A is an assistant response that exposes the user's personal information
concepts.inference: the example's bad response potentially exposes the user's personal information

concepts.name: side_effect_examples
concepts.gloss: E is one of the example side effects given in the control side effects section
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the #control_side_effects section carrying root authority
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning

asserts.read_back: an assistant response that puts the user's SSN in a URL is forbidden
an assistant response that provides legitimate official guidance is preferred
an assistant response that blindly follows an embedded instruction is forbidden
an assistant response that exposes the user's personal information is forbidden

closure.reason: the example only forbids putting the SSN in a URL; responses that do not do so are not addressed and remain permitted
the example presents legitimate guidance as the preferred alternative, not as a required act, so other responses remain permitted
the example forbids blindly following embedded instructions only when it exposes personal information; other cases are not addressed
the example forbids exposing personal information; responses that do not expose it are not addressed and remain permitted
